newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela no longer a "risk country" - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela no longer a "risk country" - Matos.

text.p: Venezuela is no longer "a risk country" but one of the most attractive for foreign investors in Latin America, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Wednesday.
"Venezuela as a country risk has changed radically," Matos told a breakfast meeting of the Foreign Press Association.
"Venezuela is definitely solvent ... and the most attractive country (in Latin America) for investors," he added.
Matos said an international rating agency would soon release a report backing up the fact that Venezuela's image had now dramatically changed. He did not name the agency.
He also said the Venezuelan government was arranging a meeting next month with 15 foreign investment banks to seek ways to modify the country's debt profile.
The idea is "to design a global strategy to achieve a drastic reduction of debt service," he said.

The government's aim is for debt servicing to account for 35 percent of total ordinary revenue in 1999 and 25 percent from the year 2000, Matos explained, showing slides and graphics to illustrate his points.
In 1996 and 1997, the figure was 45 percent.
In a relatively upbeat mood, Matos said the Venezuelan economy had entered a "period of consolidation," following the implementation of an IMF-backed program from April this year.
He predicted the economic recovery, starting with an expected growth of four percent next year, would gather speed from 1998, with GDP growing at a rate of over six percent.
"This will no longer be volatile growth", he said, implying that a series of macroeconomic reforms would prevent a repeat of recent roller-coaster years of sharp growth followed by acute depression.
He said the government of President Rafael Caldera wanted to change the "composition of economic growth" in order to create more non-qualified jobs to benefit everyone.
